findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handlers licenses to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, management will take the steps to ensure all food handling staff has the required food handlers license. Ensure all food handling employees has the required food handlers license within 30 days of employment.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: Observed store to not have proper Norovirus paperwork. SCDPH provided PIC with information on Norovirus prevention. Ensure Norovirus clean up policy is available in facility. 
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (REPEAT) Ice machine observed to have an accumulation of mold in and around the chute. PIC was instructed to clean ice machine. Ensure ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent mold accumulation. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-702.11: Observed wiping cloth stored on counter used to clean off turkey from meat slicer. Cloth was soiled from previous use and was not stored in a proper sanitizer solution. Ensure that a proper sanitizer bucket is prepared and any potential cloths used for sanitizing are kept inside bucket. These cloths should be used to clean equipment between uses. In addition, meat slicer is in use throughout the day, this slicer should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours. During inspection, CK had conversation with PIC regarding sanitizer bucket creation and PIC opted to using their triple sink in the moment. 
4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. 
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (REPEAT) (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses for the facility. Multiple employees work for the location, but there are no copies of food handler’s licenses available. Discussed with PIC. Ensure copies of food handler’s licenses are readily available in the public health folder. Ensure staff obtains a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. License is valid for 3 years. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed a food handling employee to wash hands and turn faucet off without a barrier. Employee then went to wash dishes at the 3 compartment sink. Inspector stopped employee and discussed proper hand washing technique. PIC was present and overheard the discussion. Ensure employee properly wash hands with warm water, soap, lather for 15 seconds, then rinse with warm water, dry hands with paper towel, and turn off faucets with a barrier such as a the used paper towel. Barrier use with the faucets allows for less cross contamination. Employee re-washed hands. PIC was noted to understand proper hand washing techniques. Ensure active managerial controls are administered to monitor employee hand washing. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the interior of the ice machine (inside ceiling and sides) to have accumulation of mold. Mold is present where ice falls from the interior of the machine into the basin. Inspector showed PIC. Ice machine is relatively new per PIC. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean the interior of the ice machine. Inspector showed PIC where the mold was growing in the machine. Facility employees began to remove ice from the ice machine. Do not use this ice - discard. Inspector will follow-up regarding cleaning of ice machine on 11/3/23.

(REPEAT) Observed the shelves of the walk-in cooler to be soiled with white accumulations. PIC was instructed to clean the facility often enough to prevent accumulation of substances on shelving units. Ensure shelving units are washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Discussed with PIC. Repeat from last routine inspection on 9/21/22.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

No procedures or kit were available for cleaning of vomit or diarrheal events at the facility. The CDC procedure given out by SCDPH was given to correct the violation. Items needed to utilize this procedure are available around the facility. PIC instructed to ensure that employees/management are aware of what the procedures are and/or where the physical copy of the procedure is located for if the situation occurs.

Multiple locations on the walls and shelves of the walk in cooler are observed with white and dark green accumulations. PIC is instructed to clean the facility often enough to prevent accumulation of deleterious substances.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

A can of Java Monster is observed open and partial consumed on a shelf in the walk in cooler next to and above foods intended for consumer use. A conversation took place with the PIC and that are aware that personal foods/drinks should be maintained separated form foods intended for consumers. Suggestions included placing employee consumables below and away from food or in a pan labeled “Employees”. The can was removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM.

Multiple Foodborne Illness Risk Factor Violations observed during the inspection indicating poor knowledge/ training practices. Ensure the person in charge is aware of food code requirements and is enforcing requirements related to the facility of the 2017 Food Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM is available during the inspection. As a Class-II facility, this location is required to have a Certified Food Protection Manager on site at all times that they are operating. PIC is instructed ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

PIC at the facility is unaware of any reporting agreements filled for the facility. The manager was contacted during the inspection and they were also not aware of any paperwork needed for employee illness. Documentation from both the 2018 and 2019 routine inspections indicate that PICs were notified of the requirement and given copies of  the Sangamon County Reporting Agreements at both inspection. Another copy is being given during this inspection and the facility is instructed to maintain records at the facility moving forward.
